title: Optimize Workbench: recommendation cards, diff review, and reconciliation trail
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: customers need a low-friction way to evaluate batching/caching recommendations and safely apply or revert configuration changes from the Optimize console while preserving a clear audit trail for compliance. Current console previews are terse, lack contextual cost deltas, and offer limited visibility after apply.

Objective: build an 'Optimize Workbench' UX that surfaces recommendation cards with concise cost/latency tradeoffs, an interactive diff review that highlights concrete config changes and estimated impact, and a reconciliation trail that records all apply/rollback events with metadata for audits and post-change verification. The Workbench should be usable by platform engineers and PMs, support canary/staged applies, and integrate with existing RBAC and KMS audits.

Scope: recommendation card layout, diff preview panel (side-by-side and inline), apply flow with safety checks and canary options, reconciliation trail (searchable, filterable, exportable), telemetry events for evaluation and post-apply regressions.

Out of scope: backend model recommendation algorithms (handled by Optimize engine), dedicated capacity autoscaling controls (separate project), and multi-tenant billing changes (handled by Billing team).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Each recommendation card displays: succinct title, primary metric (estimated monthly USD delta), secondary metric (median latency percent change), confidence score, and links to sample prompts affected.
AC2: Selecting 'Review diff' opens an interactive diff panel showing before/after config JSON with line-level highlights, annotated rationale, and an estimated cost/latency delta per changed key.

AC3: Apply flow requires: (a) explicit confirmation, (b) optional canary percentage and duration, (c) dependency checks and dry-run validation; successful apply emits a reconciliation record containing user, timestamp, target scope, canary settings, and pre-apply snapshot.
AC4: Reconciliation trail supports filtering by user, date range, target model/route, and outcome (applied/rolled back/failed) and allows CSV export of visible rows.

AC5: Rollback action is visible on reconciliation entries; initiating rollback triggers safety validation, produces its own reconciliation entry, and returns the system to the recorded pre-apply snapshot within the canary SLA where possible.
AC6: Telemetry events emitted for preview, apply, rollback, and canary completion; dashboards surface pre/post cost and latency comparisons for the impacted routes within 24 hours.
AC7: Feature gated behind 'optimize.workbench' feature flag and available in console-2025.03 release candidate for internal dogfooding.
notes: 2025-02-28 - Discovery: gathered interviews with three platform customers and internal SREs; main pain points were lack of readable diffs and no single source of truth after apply.
2025-03-01 - Design spike: low-fidelity mock uploaded to Figma (see links). Decision to use side-by-side diff with inline annotations rather than a purely summarized delta to aid audits.
2025-03-03 - PM review: prioritized reconciliation trail over complex multi-target batching in MVP to reduce scope and hit audit expectations.
2025-03-04 - Engineering sync: ENG estimates 5 points; backend needs reconciliation table and snapshot API; dependency on ENG-41877 for snapshot storage schema.
2025-03-05 - Security consult: requested KMS access pattern review and confirmation that reconciliation entries are immutable once sealed; security review required before GA.
Design feedback: prefer cost deltas shown with color-coding and confidence ribbons; include quick links to run a targeted eval for affected prompts.
Post-launch followups: add pre-apply automated canary metrics (smoke checks) and optional rollback-on-anomaly policy in the next iteration.
security_notes: Reconciliation entries must be write-once and signed with customer-scoped key material. Access to apply/rollback actions gated by RBAC role 'optimize_admin'. Logging must include KMS key reference and requestor IP for compliance audits.
qa_plan: Manual test: create a batching recommendation, review diff, apply with 10% canary for 1 hour, validate reconciliation entry created and canary metrics recorded.
Manual test: attempt apply without permission and assert action blocked and audit log created.
Automated test: snapshot -> apply -> simulate anomaly -> trigger rollback -> verify state matches pre-apply snapshot within canary SLA.
E2E smoke: UI rendering of recommendation cards on large result sets (>200 cards) remains responsive with lazy loading.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal dogfood): enable feature flag for internal orgs and select beta customers; monitor reconciliation events and telemetry for two weeks.
Phase 2 (beta): open to all paid customers with console-2025.03 release; require opt-in via workspace settings and email notifications for applies.
Phase 3 (GA): enable by default with admin-level controls and long-term retention toggle for reconciliation records.
Rollback strategy: feature flag off will hide apply buttons and preserve existing runtime configs; reconciliation trail remains readable for forensic investigations.
